items.title: Jeva: System One Models from First Principles
items.summary: System one models enable direct, low-latency decision-making. Yet recent practice of predicting an answer from serialized text does not, by itself, respect the structure of a decision problem. We argue that current designs underemphasize four important structural requirements. items.title: Agent-Reflex: Teaching Language Agents to Act Reflectively
items.summary: Large language models have evolved from single-turn chatbots into interactive agents capable of long-horizon reasoning. In real deployments, MCP tool services can return noisy feedback and users may intervene to correct the agent, but existing methods provide limited supervision for reflection learning and failure recovery. To bridge this gap, we propose Agent-Reflex, a general training framework for incentivizing proactive reflection in agents.

items.title: Urbex: Agentic Spatial Grounding for City-Scale 3D Scenes
items.summary: City-scale 3D grounding is commonly formulated as candidate ranking, which requires precomputed instance proposals and becomes inefficient in large outdoor scenes. We propose Urbex, an agentic vision-language framework that instead casts grounding as active spatial search. items.summary: Long-horizon agents have drawn growing attention for their ability to work autonomously -- from hours to days -- on economically valuable tasks, a capability essential to automated discovery and recursive self-improvement (RSI). items.title: GreenWAM: A World Foundation Model for Robotics
items.summary: A robot needs a world model that predicts how its actions will change the scene and a policy that chooses those actions. Models are usually built and evaluated for only one of these roles, and every robot records its actions in its own format. We ask whether one robot world model can serve both roles across different bodies, and what makes this work. items.title: Last Secure Code Benchmark: Is the Code You Vibe Secure?
items.summary: AI coding agents now write much of the code that ships, yet whether that code is secure remains unclear. We introduce the Last Secure Code Benchmark, a comprehensive evaluation of secure code generation by coding agents. items.summary: Determining whether an image is AI-generated does not establish whether the situation it depicts is factually supported. items.title: APEX: Asynchronous Prefix Denoising for Extreme Compression
items.summary: Fewer latent tokens promise cheaper diffusion. Yet aggressive latent compression creates a reconstruction-generation dilemma: adding channels improves reconstruction but makes generation harder. items.summary: Recent video super-resolution (VSR) models achieve efficient one-step generation through diffusion distillation. items.summary: On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) trains a large language model using supervision from a teacher instantiated from the same model as the student. items.summary: Vision-language navigation requires agents to follow natural-language instructions to reach target locations, making high-quality language supervision essential. items.title: ReTerm: Recovery Training for Self-Improving Terminal Agents
items.summary: Terminal agents have shown strong abilities in complex coding tasks. However, they often struggle to recover from errors during long-running execution (e.g., command errors, faulty implementations), eventually leading to task failures. items.summary: Reliable video reasoning requires models to produce correct answers and expose supporting visual evidence. items.summary: Latent diffusion models enable high-quality video generation, but video VAE encoding and decoding remain computationally expensive. items.title: LifeSearch: Benchmarking Deep Research Agents for Real-World Life and Productivity
items.summary: Deep research (DR) agents address open-ended information needs through multi-step reasoning, long-horizon web search, and evidence synthesis. items.summary: Reconstructing complete, high-quality meshes of large-scale scenes from unposed multi-view images requires faithful geometric grounding while plausibly completing surfaces that are unobserved or only sparsely captured.
